articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: Video showed thick smoke rising from the plane crash of the Boeing 767 that the Federal Aviation Administration says overran the airport runway in Miami.
articles.title: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport

articles.author: Esme Nicholson
articles.description: Exit polls show Germany's AfD taking a commanding lead in a regional election, but it remains unclear whether the far-right party can form the country's first state government since World War II.
articles.title: German exit polls suggest far-right party has big lead in regional election

articles.author: Ulaa Kuziez
articles.description: Even as anti-Muslim rhetoric rises in Texas, Muslim pitmasters are winning over diners and reshaping one of the state's most iconic culinary traditions.
articles.title: American Muslims are giving Texas barbecue a halal makeover

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held meetings in Kyiv with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy on Sunday, a day after lengthy conversations with Russian President Putin in Moscow.
articles.title: Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after Moscow Putin meeting

articles.author: Malaka Gharib
articles.description: Learn a few surprising facts about procrastination — and helpful tools to overcome it — with this quiz. It's based on social scientist Itamar Shatz's new book, Solving Procrastination.
articles.title: QUIZ: Ugh, I'll do it later. How much do you know about procrastination?

articles.author: Laurel Dalrymple
articles.description: We asked readers to share stories about a moment of kindness involving a stranger. Here are some of their heartwarming anecdotes.
articles.title: Whatever happened to kindness? Spoiler alert: Our readers prove it's alive and well

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.title: U.S. and Iran trade attacks on ships as fighting flares up again

articles.author: Ali Asif Shawon
articles.description: It was a light bulb moment: If monsoon rains keep kids from safely getting to school, let's create a floating school to pick them up! Bangladesh pioneered the idea. How's it doing?
articles.title: Whatever happened to the floating schools of Bangladesh?

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.
articles.title: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine

articles.author: Linda Holmes
articles.description: NPR's Linda Holmes is a daily puzzle devotee. She recommends games that will test your knowledge of geography, history, and even the most obscure corners of Wikipedia.
articles.title: If you prefer puzzles to doomscrolling, here are 5 great games to check out

articles.author: Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

One Nation has come up with a plan to give people their superannuation earlier, reducing the amount they’ll have at retirement in exchange for a current cash boost.
Pauline Hanson says under their plan anyone paying rent or a mortgage can take up to a quarter of their super as a “pay boost” for up to three years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia politics live: Median full-time worker to be $25,000 worse off under Hanson’s super plan, peak body says

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Row centres on stake held by Patarkatsishvili family in bottled water firm it jointly owns with Russian oligarch
A British theatre impresario and her billionaire family are embroiled in a bitter dispute with Ukrainian authorities seeking to seize a water company they jointly own with a Russian oligarch.
The row centres on a 34% stake held in the producer of Ukraine’s biggest bottled water brands by the Patarkatsishvili family, including Liana Patarkatsishvili, who recently worked on an immersive show with Toby Jones and Meera Syal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine seeks to seize water company owned by billionaire family of British theatre mogul

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: UN special rapporteur on occupied territories says ban on goods from settlements ‘important’ but must go further if it is to amount to more than a ‘press release’
The UK’s planned ban on trade with unlawful Israeli settlements is a welcome, if overdue, first step and must be judged according to its practical impact, a UN expert has told the Guardian.
The UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has vowed to act more decisively against Israeli settlements, as well as continued restrictions of aid into Gaza, prompting the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, to claim on Saturday that Downing Street was motivated by “Jew hatred”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN expert Francesca Albanese calls for ‘true paradigm shift’ as Miliband resets policy on Israel

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Firms are more likely to use technology as ‘the intern in the office’ than as a replacement for skilled staff
Professional designers should not feel “threatened” by the rapid growth of generative AI, according to business leaders, despite fears over job losses in the sector.
With design and film production companies and manufacturers all adopting AI at an accelerating pace, industry bodies said the technology would be used to enhance the work of designers rather than replace them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Designers should not fear being replaced by AI, industry leaders say

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Ashlyn Nassif, daughter of Toplace boss who fled Australia in 2022, has pleaded guilty to providing false or misleading information to obtain loan from Westpac

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The daughter of a fugitive property developer succumbed to pressure from her father when she falsified documents for a $150m construction loan, a Sydney court has heard.
Ashlyn Nassif, the daughter of Jean Nassif, pleaded guilty in June to providing false or misleading information to obtain the loan from Westpac, which was used to construct three apartment towers in Sydney’s north-west in 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jean Nassif’s daughter tells court father ‘pressured’ her to falsify documents for $150m construction loan

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett and Catie McLeod
articles.description:
Sydney-headquartered group suspends work on some of its 45 construction sites affecting 60% of workforce

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than 200 workers at Sydney-headquartered Bathla Group have been stood down as administrators of the embattled property developer seek emergency funds to stave off a company-wide collapse.
The insolvency advisory Teneo said on Monday that new short-term funding arrangements would only allow Bathla to continue construction on some of its 45 construction sites, though it did not identify which projects were being prioritised.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than 200 people stood down at embattled housing developer Bathla amid $3.4bn debt

articles.author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
articles.description:
Alternative für Deutschland surges to victory in Saxony-Anhalt as Friedrich Merz’s CDU slumps to disastrous result 

AfD thanks Elon Musk as France warns state election win a ‘serious moment’

The populist, far-right, anti-immigration Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has surged to a resounding victory in a crucial state election in Germany, but fell just short of winning a majority in its quest to form the country’s first far-right state government since the second world war.
The party of Germany’s unpopular chancellor Friedrich Merz, the Christian Democrats (CDU), slumped to a disastrous result in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right AfD wins key German state election but falls just short of majority

articles.author: Diane Taylor and Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Influencer livestreams event calling for men to travel to port to block coaches carrying asylum seekers from leaving
Hundreds of far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast. The vessel’s arrival sparked a major response with a helicopter, an aeroplane and lifeboats sent to the scene.
It is thought to be the first time such a large boat containing asylum seekers has been brought to Portsmouth and the first time a large group of anti-migrant protesters have tried to block newly arrived asylum seekers from being processed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds of far-right protesters descend on Portsmouth after small boat arrival

articles.author: Staff and agencies
articles.description:
Lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt welcomes further ‘strong’ cooperation with Musk as French minister says ‘we cannot forget our history’

AfD wins key German state election but falls just short of majority

The candidate who led the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party to a historic state election victory in Germany has thanked Elon Musk for his support, as one French minister warned that this was a “serious moment” for Europe.
The AfD more than doubled its support in the Saxony-Anhalt region and appears to be on the brink of becoming the first far-right party to gain power in Germany at state level since the second world war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Germany’s far-right AfD thanks Elon Musk as France warns state election win a ‘serious moment’

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Oscar-winning actor says she and other outspoken critics of Israel have found it ‘impossible’ to get hired by major studios
The Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon has said she is still losing work because of her outspoken support for Palestinians, despite what she ⁠described as a broader shift ⁠in public opinion against ​US support for Israel.
Speaking at the Venice film festival, where she is promoting her latest movie The Echo Chamber, Sarandon said some parts of the film industry continued to ⁠shun her over her activism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Susan Sarandon says she is losing movie roles because of her support for Palestine

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus near to station will make it easier for students and staff to commute
Not so long ago, the first impression for visitors arriving by train to Bristol’s main railway station was a derelict building described by David Cameron as looking like the entrance to a war zone.
On Monday, a shiny new University of Bristol campus on the site of that crumbling Royal Mail sorting office next door to Temple Meads is opening its doors to students, teachers and members of the public.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gigantic spaceship’: University of Bristol’s flagship £500m campus opens

articles.author: Diana Ramirez-Simon and agencies
articles.description:
Armed suspect Patrick Havas allegedly attacked Amy Acton during a campaign stop at a fair, injuring several people
Amy Acton, Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, was the target of an attack on Sunday during a campaign stop at the Canfield Fair, campaign officials said. Several people were injured when the armed assailant lunged at Acton.
The suspect knocked volunteers to the ground before he was arrested and was “discovered to have weapons”, Mahoning county Democratic party chairperson Chris Anderson said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Assailant lunged at Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, campaign says

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Three people in critical condition and two hospitalized as operations at one of busiest US airports brought to a halt
An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami international airport in Florida on Sunday afternoon after the flight, which was arriving from Puerto Rico, overshot the runway, striking several vehicles and resulting in at least five deaths.
The plane erupted in flames as dark smoke billowed into the sky, bringing operations at one of the busiest airports in the US to a halt. The pilot and copilot were trapped in the cockpit as a result of the crash, said the Miami-Dade rescue fire chief Ray Jadallah.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport

articles.author: Ben Doherty, Andy Ball and Nick Evershed
articles.description:
Exclusive: US-controlled weapons corporations and forces have control or access to more than 100 facilities across the continent, which some analysts describe as a ‘colonisation’ of Australia’s military. Find a map of them here

US military presence in Australia, mapped – video

Why can the US access so many Australian military bases? – podcast

US military interests control or have access to more than 100 defence facilities on Australian soil, in what some analysts describe as a “saturation” – even a “colonisation” – of the Australian continent.
New data compiled by the Nautilus Institute and published by Guardian Australia maps the extent of US militarisation. The US military controls 17 facilities on mainland Australia and has access to 75 more Australian-run military installations. US defence corporations have access to an additional 18.
Gathering intelligence, accessing satellite data for targeting information and communications intercepts.
Training, including for 2,500 marines on dry-season rotation in the Northern Territory.
Pre-positioning warfighting assets such as Osprey aircraft.
Logistics hubs holding weapons, munitions and fuel, stored in case of a war in the Pacific.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US now has access to more than half Australia’s military bases – could it drag the country unwillingly into war?

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Storm, which may make impact as soon as Monday, is third system in weeks to threaten state during hurricane season
Hawaii has declared a state of emergency as powerful Hurricane Lowell makes its way toward the islands, with the first impacts expected as soon as Monday.
The storm is the third system in just over three weeks to threaten Hawaii during an active hurricane season in the central Pacific. Lowell remained a category 3 hurricane early on Sunday morning, packing winds of 125 miles per hour while moving north-west at six miles per hour.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hawaii declares state of emergency as Hurricane Lowell approaches islands

articles.author: Jack Larkin
articles.description:
The casket, grown from mycelium and hemp fibres, takes just 45 days to break down, enriching the soil in the process

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman has been buried in a coffin made from mushrooms in New South Wales in an eco-friendly first for Australia.
Carolyn, whose surname was withheld for privacy reasons, was laid to rest on Friday by friends and family at Springwood Cemetery in the Blue Mountains. She was aged in her 70s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Woman laid to rest in coffin made from mushrooms in Australian first

articles.author: Amy Hawkins in Kyiv
articles.description:
Witkoff says he hopes trilateral talks involving the US, Ukraine and Europe will be announced ‘in short order’
The US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to Ukraine for the first time on Sunday for talks with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in an attempt to end the war with Russia.
The Ukrainian president announced plans to widen peace discussions to include European countries in the near future, saying he wanted to do “everything to ensure that trilateral meetings take place” with Ukraine, the US and Europe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff visit Kyiv for first time after Putin talks

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Chris Wright tells ABC there ‘may not’ be an agreement that would prevent Iran from having nuclear weapons
US energy secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday morning that the US may not be able to reach a nuclear agreement with Iran that would prevent the country from having nuclear weapons.
Asked on ABC on Sunday morning about any sign of such a deal, as negotiations appear stalled and the US-Israel war on Iran continues, Wright said: “There may not be a nuclear agreement.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy secretary says US might not reach nuclear agreement with Iran

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state
A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaica over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said.
The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Protest using 10 coffins to symbolise struggling manufacturing industry to take place in Brussels
Job losses in EU manufacturing will rapidly increase unless Brussels stops the “colonisation” of industry by Chinese component manufacturers, a leading industry trade body has warned.
Eurometal predicts 300,000 job losses in manufacturing in the rest of 2026 because of expanding competition from China, which is now enjoying a record €1bn-a-day trade surplus with the bloc.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU faces 300,000 factory job cuts as China ‘colonises’ supply chains, industry warns

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and agency
articles.description:
Legal fight continues as states begin sending out ballots for voters to vote by mail in November’s midterm elections
The Trump administration renewed its appeal to the US supreme court on Sunday to allow restrictions on mail-in voting, after a federal judge had blocked new limits on such ballots, just ahead of November’s midterm elections.
The latest filing follows a decision by US district court judge Indira Talwani on Friday to extend a court order preventing the US Postal Service (USPS) from enforcing Donald Trump’s executive order.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump again asks supreme court to restrict mail-in voting as midterms loom

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Schools and councils express financial concerns as EHCP applications surge before potential change in provision

‘Powerful example’: minister looks to Essex school for blueprint to transform Send provision

Schools and councils across England are expecting the proportion of children with special needs plans to double to one in 10, with families rushing to secure support before ministers bring in changes.
Headteachers have reported an “unreal” surge in applications for education, health and care plans (EHCPs) mandating support for needs or disabilities such as speech and learning difficulties, autism or ADHD. In 2025, just one in 20 school-age children had EHCPs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pupils with Send plans in England likely to double to one in 10 in rush for support

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves
China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth.
A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China prepares £40bn stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth

articles.author: Ben Doherty
articles.description:
David Shoebridge says ‘words are just distractions’ until government takes action

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Greens have criticised inflammatory statements from the former Israel Defense Forces officer who ordered the attack that killed Zomi Frankcom, accusing the Albanese government of weakness over its failure to halt military exports and impose new sanctions.
Australian aid worker Frankcom and six of her colleagues were killed in 2024 while bringing food to the people of Gaza. Former IDF reserve colonel Nochi Mendel has said he would do “exactly the same thing” again and that those killed in the World Central Kitchen (WCK) humanitarian convoy in Gaza were “not innocent”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Greens criticise Labor after former IDF officer’s ‘reprehensible’ comments on Zomi Frankcom strike

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Ash cloud from Anak Krakatau affects hundreds of flights and some school and  fishing activities
Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international hub, affecting hundreds of flights as a result of an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano.
Saturday’s eruption, which produced lava and booming sounds that were heard up to 435 miles (700km) away, according to Indonesia’s geology agency, also interrupted some school activities and fishing. Two more eruptions were recorded on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Volcanic eruption halts flights at Jakarta and seven other Indonesian airports

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Far-right linked group able to mobilise at scale due to police ‘inaction’, says founder of Hope Not Hate
The group of masked, black-clad vigilantes who blockaded roads in Dover could repeat the disruption unless police step up efforts to stop them, politicians and campaigners have said.
Responsibility for the demonstration has been claimed by Patriot Platform, an anti-immigration group with links to the far right, which styles itself as having a “fierce love for our homeland”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black-clad Dover vigilantes will return if police do not act, say campaigners

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Tan Dhesi says Argentinian threats make it more crucial than ever that PM increase defence spending
Javier Milei’s threats to the Falkland Islands make it even more important that Andy Burnham increase defence spending immediately, according to the Labour chair of the defence committee.
Tan Dhesi said the comments by the Argentinian president this week show why the government should raise military spending to 3% of GDP by 2030. But he said Burnham’s plans remain mired in confusion after the prime minister appeared to reassure him that the 2030 target would be hit, only for Downing Street to later retreat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falklands row shows urgent need to commit to 3% target, says Labour defence committee chair

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Taraneh Rahimi was told prison guards would rape her sister, Romina, if she did not sign a confession
The twins were 19 and still in high school when they were taken from their beds in the dead of night by masked men later identified as being sent by the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.
After four months of desperately seeking news from hospitals and state institutions, their mother, Marzieh Nourmohammadi, finally learned their fate. Taraneh and Romina Rahimi had been seized over their decision to join millions on the streets of Iranian cities during the January protests against the regime. The twins were unrecognisable by the time of their mother’s prison visit in May.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Broken feet, ripped-out hair and now a death sentence: the fate of twin sisters jailed over Iran protests

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president suggests he might support his Argentinian ally’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands
Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House.
It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s pique with UK could lead to favor to acolyte Milei over Falklands

articles.author: Associated Press in Bogotá
articles.description:
Officials accuse National Liberation Army of launching strike followed by clash inside military compound
An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compound in north-eastern Colombia has killed at least three soldiers and wounded four, Colombia’s army said on Saturday.
Local authorities blamed the attack – which took place late on Friday – on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drone attack blamed on guerrillas kills at least three soldiers in Colombia

articles.author: AFP in Cairo
articles.description:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffic drugs
An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and agencies
articles.description:
Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US
The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”.
According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US military says it struck three Iranian tankers after American warships came under missile attack

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Houthi rebel offensive against government forces on west coast leads to some of deadliest clashes in years
Clashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel movement have killed more than 60 people, including civilians, as the Houthis pushed forward with a military offensive on Yemen’s western coast.
Twenty-six government troops and 31 Houthi fighters were killed during several hours of fighting in the country’s south-west on Saturday, medical and military sources told Agence France-Presse (AFP). A missile strike also killed six civilians and injured seven others travelling by bus in the city of Taiz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Civilians among at least 60 killed in Yemen as ground fighting escalates

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Carlos de Almeida Baptista Júnior describes 2022 meeting in new book as ex-leader’s son vies with Lula for presidency
The far-right populist Jair Bolsonaro was in his final days as Brazil’s president when, six weeks after losing the election and still refusing to recognise the result, he summoned the heads of the armed forces to a meeting.
The defence minister, Gen Paulo Sérgio Nogueira de Oliveira, took out a document from a plastic folder and handed copies to the commanders of the navy, army and air force.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It cost me many friendships’: former Brazil military chief reveals inside struggle to stop Bolsonaro’s coup

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland
The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.
In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped at depth of 170 metres
Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped.
The workers were rescued during an operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst affected by last week’s floods, according to the army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after Nepal-Tibet floods

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Seoul reportedly seeking parliamentary approval to send military assets to Middle East but president’s office plays down claims
South Korea is reviewing a possible deployment of military assets to the strait of Hormuz amid pressure from Donald Trump over Seoul’s reluctance to provide support in the region, according to domestic media reports.
Citing unnamed government and military sources, the reports published on Thursday and Friday said preparations were under way and that the government intended to seek parliamentary approval for a new deployment. The reports, which appeared in major South Korean outlets, said the exact scale and timing had not been agreed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea pushes back on reports it is readying Hormuz deployment amid US pressure

articles.author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
articles.description:
Pedro Sánchez continues to defend Rabat after police report claiming border forces helped 70,000 cross border

Europe live – latest updates

Spain has seen no evidence “whatsoever” that Morocco planned or facilitated a mass border breach into its north African territory of Ceuta, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has told parliament.
The address on Thursday followed the emergence of a police report, commissioned by a judge and widely quoted in the media, claiming Moroccan border forces had actively aided about 70,000 people to cross the border in late July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence ‘whatsoever’ Morocco behind Ceuta border breach

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border

After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts

Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.
Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Sharpeville
articles.description:
Claim relating to 1960 attack on hundreds of protesters part of wave of litigation over apartheid crimes in South Africa
The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be.
Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress (ANC). “The weather was very nice, the sun was out. You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We continue to suffer’: victims of apartheid-era Sharpeville massacre demand compensation

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site
Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.
Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Referendum result means fewer seats in parliament and new rules on candidates, ahead of December elections
Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution, which critics say will undermine democracy, that significantly expands presidential powers ahead of elections due in December.
According to provisional results, 70% of voters approved sweeping changes in the tiny west African state’s first constitutional amendment since revisions that ended the one-party socialist state more than three decades ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New constitution in Guinea-Bissau will undermine democracy, opponents say

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Several missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38

Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far

A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found.
Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Relief as five Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive

articles.author: Angus Thomson
articles.description:
More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000, including 36 British nationals, remain missing
A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight.
Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British aid worker mistakenly identified as a survivor of Nepal-Tibet disaster

articles.author: Diana Ramirez-Simon and agencies
articles.description:
Armed suspect Patrick Havas allegedly attacked Amy Acton during a campaign stop at a fair, injuring several people
Amy Acton, Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, was the target of an attack on Sunday during a campaign stop at the Canfield Fair, campaign officials said. Several people were injured when the armed assailant lunged at Acton.
The suspect knocked volunteers to the ground before he was arrested and was “discovered to have weapons”, Mahoning county Democratic party chairperson Chris Anderson said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Assailant lunged at Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, campaign says

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and agency
articles.description:
Legal fight continues as states begin sending out ballots for voters to vote by mail in November’s midterm elections
The Trump administration renewed its appeal to the US supreme court on Sunday to allow restrictions on mail-in voting, after a federal judge had blocked new limits on such ballots, just ahead of November’s midterm elections.
The latest filing follows a decision by US district court judge Indira Talwani on Friday to extend a court order preventing the US Postal Service (USPS) from enforcing Donald Trump’s executive order.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump again asks supreme court to restrict mail-in voting as midterms loom

articles.author: Lok Darjee
articles.description:
Montana’s Sam Forstag says US working class is left playing a game of chance while neither party serves its interests
At around five o’clock on a winter evening in 2013, then college student Sam Forstag was driving through a snowstorm toward his third job of the day, making sandwiches at the Subway inside a Walmart.
“I was always late,” Forstag recalled with a laugh more than a decade later.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: This smokejumper says the US has lost its empathy. That’s why he’s running for Congress

articles.author: Chris Stein
articles.description:
Trump is unpopular and inflation is still high – and Democrats are looking to use that to their advantage
When voters went to the polls in the 2022 midterm elections, all the ingredients were there for Joe Biden’s allies to suffer a wipeout. The president was unpopular, inflation was high and historical trends predicted voters would take out their frustrations by ending the Democratic party’s control of Congress.
But when the ballots were tallied, the gains Republicans expected to make did not quite materialize. They had won the House of Representatives, but only by a slim margin, while Democrats had expanded their majority in the Senate and built up their strength in state legislatures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Game on: November elections kick into high gear with control of Congress in the balance

articles.author: William Christou and agencies
articles.description:
Donald Trump’s business ally and son-in-law now heading from Moscow to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Kyiv for the first time in their roles as Donald Trump’s peace envoys to Ukraine, after talks on Saturday in Moscow.
The White House said Witkoff and Kushner had “discussed substantive plans for next steps” towards ending the war between Ukraine and Russia during their meeting on Saturday in Moscow with Vladimir Putin.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Witkoff and Kushner discussed ‘next steps’ with Putin to end Ukraine war, says US

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Todd Blanche’s remarks are part of a totally-not-invented moral panic that stretches the limits of the imagination
Being a public school teacher in the US these days is tough. You’ve got to pay for a lot of your own supplies, deal with smartphone-addicted children and perform gender-affirming surgeries on your lunch break.
Luckily our intrepid attorney general, Todd Blanche, is on the case. Blanche appeared on Fox News this week to decry a “pandemic” of gender transitions in schools across the US. “There’s not a parent in America, no matter where you live, that would want their school to change and call their child by a different name and not expect to be told about that. We partnered with the Department of Education recently to combat this very trend and, really, pandemic that’s happening in some school districts around the country,” Blanche said. He seemed more concerned with name changes than with surgery, but the president himself has suggested on several occasions that schools are furtively doing surgery on children. During a campaign speech in 2024, for example, Donald Trump said: “Can you imagine … your son leaves the house and you say: ‘Jimmy, I love you so much. Go have a good day in school,’ and your son comes back with a brutal operation? Can you even imagine this?”
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US attorney general is fretting about a ‘pandemic’ of gender transitions in schools | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
The US defense secretary faces internal dissent and discord at the Pentagon, accused of focusing on culture war issues and his own political ambitions as the Iran war drags on
In a different Washington, under a different president, a return to the well-worn playbook of all-out sanctions to counter Iran might have been the signal for a publicity-hungry US secretary of defense to adopt a lower profile.
But these are no ordinary times. And Pete Hegseth is no ordinary defense secretary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Captain calamity: Pete Hegseth under fire for ‘inept’ leadership of US military

articles.author: Alice Speri
articles.description:
Progressive candidates navigate their ties to the DSA as the group faces historic growth and mounting pressure
Days before he won the Democratic primary for a US Senate seat in Michigan, insurgent newcomer Abdul El-Sayed was asked whether he was concerned about being labeled a “socialist”.
“I’d rather think of myself as a capitalist who has actually read about capitalism,” El-Sayed told CBS News anchor Ed O’Keefe. “I’m not a socialist.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Leftist insurgents are storming the midterms – just don’t call them all democratic socialists

articles.author: Jonathan Freedland
articles.description:
Such is the US president’s narcissism that he would see a Democratic victory as proof that he’s indispensable – meanwhile, his every decision spells calamity for voters
What is Donald Trump playing at? If it’s true that the best way of understanding the behaviour of an organisation is to assume it’s controlled by a secret cabal of its enemies, perhaps that same logic extends to the current conduct of the president of the United States. Maybe he secretly wants Republicans to lose the looming midterm elections that will decide the balance of power in the US for the next two years and for which the first postal ballots were sent out today.
That’s not as mad a theory as it sounds. Indeed, there are at least two reasons why Trump might either be unbothered by Republican defeat in November or even covertly desire it. We’ll come to those, but let’s start with a pattern of behaviour that is hard to explain as anything other than calculated self-sabotage.
Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How much does Donald Trump care about winning the midterms? Apparently, not much at all | Jonathan Freedland

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Believed to be first US deportations to fourth country, six face ‘horrific conditions’ in Equatorial Guinea, say lawyers
In late August, around 20 people were put on a flight in the US, shackled at the wrists, waist and ankles, and sent to Liberia as part of one of the largest third-country deportation arrangements of Donald Trump’s second term.
Although more than 23,000 people have been sent to 26 countries other than their own since last year, that day saw something that had not happened before: six people refused to get off the plane – and were instead taken to another country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Six people refused to get off ICE deportation plane – now they’re held in limbo in Equatorial Guinea

articles.author: Joanna Walters in New York
articles.description:
Letty Cottin Pogrebin says Steinem taught the younger feminist how to change a ‘man’s world’ not adjust to it

Gloria Steinem, groundbreaking feminist campaigner, dies aged 92

‘We badly need to raise our boys more like our girls’: Gloria Steinem – a life in quotes

When an up and coming feminist author and journalist bumped into Gloria Steinem at a women’s conference in Washington DC in 1971 she was awed but also realized she had been on the wrong track by “asking women to adjust” to “a man’s world” rather than organizing to change it, as the more senior activist of the two was doing.
Letty Cottin Pogrebin and Steinem ended up comparing notes and brainstorming until the wee hours of the following morning and Steinem asked her to come on board with a project she was cooking up – Ms magazine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Founding editor of Ms magazine on Gloria Steinem: ‘The least egomaniacal person’

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
The trillions in tax cuts going to the rich and corporations could have instead been used to address the affordability crisis
Dear reader, I recognize that your eyes might glaze over at any mention of the nation’s $40tn federal debt. But your reaction to this mind-boggling number shouldn’t be ennui; it should be outrage and dismay.
Outrage is in order because the nation’s debt has climbed to more than $40tn under Donald Trump, even though back in 2016, when the debt was less than half what it is today, candidate Trump insisted that he’d totally eliminate the debt within eight years. That was yet another example of the Demagogue-in-Chief’s willingness to say anything, no matter how insincere or untrue, to woo voters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In 2016, Trump pledged to erase the federal debt. It just hit $40tn | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The president’s call for the FCC to scrutinize Kristen Welker’s innocuous remarks is a sign of desperation
With his approval ratings tanking, the crucial midterm elections looming, and his war with Iran turning into a quagmire, Donald Trump has entered full freak-out mode.
It’s not hard to tell. Just look at what happened this week when he lashed out at Kristen Welker, the well-respected host of NBC’s Meet the Press, and one of the best-known journalists in the nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s threat against an NBC journalist is an attack on reality | Margaret Sullivan

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Dan Alexander, produced by Nada Smiljanic and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Dan Alexander of Forbes about how Donald Trump made so much money last year at the same time trade wars, military wars and a rising national debt hurt the US economy
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How did Trump get so rich? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Paul Owen ; produced by Bryony Moore ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
One of Donald Trump’s closest and most devoted aides, Natalie Harp, has faced intense media scrutiny this week, after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, name-checked her in a speech that went viral. So what do we know about Harp, who is often referred to as the ‘human printer’? And why is everybody talking about her relationship with Trump? Helen Pidd speaks to international news editor Paul Owen
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is Trump’s ‘human printer’ aide Natalie Harp suddenly in the spotlight? - The Latest

articles.author: Jonathan Freedland with Jill Lepore . Produced by Nada Smiljanic, and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
Less than three months to go until the midterms, voters are thinking about grocery prices, the Iran war and… datacentres.

This week, Jonathan Freedland speaks to historian Jill Lepore about how this latest AI backlash could influence those all-important elections in November. Are we seeing the beginning of the end of the 'artificial state'?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Historian Jill Lepore on the datacentre backlash | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Row centres on stake held by Patarkatsishvili family in bottled water firm it jointly owns with Russian oligarch
A British theatre impresario and her billionaire family are embroiled in a bitter dispute with Ukrainian authorities seeking to seize a water company they jointly own with a Russian oligarch.
The row centres on a 34% stake held in the producer of Ukraine’s biggest bottled water brands by the Patarkatsishvili family, including Liana Patarkatsishvili, who recently worked on an immersive show with Toby Jones and Meera Syal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine seeks to seize water company owned by billionaire family of British theatre mogul

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Firms are more likely to use technology as ‘the intern in the office’ than as a replacement for skilled staff
Professional designers should not feel “threatened” by the rapid growth of generative AI, according to business leaders, despite fears over job losses in the sector.
With design and film production companies and manufacturers all adopting AI at an accelerating pace, industry bodies said the technology would be used to enhance the work of designers rather than replace them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Designers should not fear being replaced by AI, industry leaders say

articles.author: Diane Taylor and Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Influencer livestreams event calling for men to travel to port to block coaches carrying asylum seekers from leaving
Hundreds of far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast. The vessel’s arrival sparked a major response with a helicopter, an aeroplane and lifeboats sent to the scene.
It is thought to be the first time such a large boat containing asylum seekers has been brought to Portsmouth and the first time a large group of anti-migrant protesters have tried to block newly arrived asylum seekers from being processed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds of far-right protesters descend on Portsmouth after small boat arrival

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus near to station will make it easier for students and staff to commute
Not so long ago, the first impression for visitors arriving by train to Bristol’s main railway station was a derelict building described by David Cameron as looking like the entrance to a war zone.
On Monday, a shiny new University of Bristol campus on the site of that crumbling Royal Mail sorting office next door to Temple Meads is opening its doors to students, teachers and members of the public.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gigantic spaceship’: University of Bristol’s flagship £500m campus opens

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Survey finds long waiting times and overcrowding have made abuse ‘routine’ part of working on hospital frontline
Nearly three-quarters of A&E staff experience violence or aggression daily or weekly, according to a survey highlighting the “appalling” abuse of NHS workers.
The Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) said understaffed and overcrowded emergency departments were contributing to increased targeting of medics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Almost 75% of A&E staff in UK face violence or aggression daily or weekly

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state
A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaica over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said.
The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Schools and councils express financial concerns as EHCP applications surge before potential change in provision

‘Powerful example’: minister looks to Essex school for blueprint to transform Send provision

Schools and councils across England are expecting the proportion of children with special needs plans to double to one in 10, with families rushing to secure support before ministers bring in changes.
Headteachers have reported an “unreal” surge in applications for education, health and care plans (EHCPs) mandating support for needs or disabilities such as speech and learning difficulties, autism or ADHD. In 2025, just one in 20 school-age children had EHCPs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pupils with Send plans in England likely to double to one in 10 in rush for support

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Far-right linked group able to mobilise at scale due to police ‘inaction’, says founder of Hope Not Hate
The group of masked, black-clad vigilantes who blockaded roads in Dover could repeat the disruption unless police step up efforts to stop them, politicians and campaigners have said.
Responsibility for the demonstration has been claimed by Patriot Platform, an anti-immigration group with links to the far right, which styles itself as having a “fierce love for our homeland”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black-clad Dover vigilantes will return if police do not act, say campaigners

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Carmaker, which is battling Trump tariffs and Chinese competitors, faces talks with union leaders and government
The government has signalled that it will not invest taxpayers’ money to limit job losses at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), after it emerged that the UK’s biggest carmaker is planning up to 4,000 redundancies.
Before crunch talks on Tuesday between JLR, union leaders and government officials, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said it was not his job to “intervene and run businesses”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No bailouts for Jaguar Land Rover amid reports of thousands of job cuts, says minister

articles.author: Josh Halliday
articles.description:
Senior Reform UK figure has faced criticism within party after post about Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee
Labour has accused Reform’s Zia Yusuf of “straightforward racism” after he suggested the party’s frontrunner to replace Keir Starmer in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection was not British.
Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia and the leader of Camden council, has been tipped as an early favourite to contest the London seat for Labour after the former prime minister’s resignation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zia Yusuf’s post about Camden council leader is ‘straightforward racism’, says minister

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Robert Jenrick says party has followed legal protocol ‘at all times’ as Met police consider launching investigation
Nigel Farage has acknowledged the overseas donation row engulfing Reform UK “looks bad” for his party but denied it had ever taken foreign money in breach of electoral law.
The Reform leader, who is battling to contain the fallout from the allegations, was asked if he could categorically rule out that foreign money had ever been funnelled to his party. He replied: “I can. Never happened.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage says overseas donation row ‘looks bad’ but denies Reform broke law

articles.author: Helena Horton and Aamna Mohdin
articles.description:
Tories and Reform hope to unseat the incumbent by tempting some Labour voters to shift to the right 
The bicycles have been brought out and eager fists are getting ready to knock on hundreds of doors as the race for one of the most sought-after jobs in British politics springs into action.
Sadiq Khan has had a vice-like grip on London, but a range of candidates hoping to unseat him in 2028 have announced themselves. The three-time mayor has been coy about whether he will stand again, and said he would make a decision next year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: London mayoral contenders limber up for a race that is Sadiq Khan’s to lose

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Most gambling websites nudge users towards accepting tracking data and harvest it before consent is given, study shows
Online bookmakers and casinos have been accused of widespread non-compliance of information privacy requirements, including “data surveillance” of customers, according to a study.
Nearly nine out of 10 (86%) licensed British gambling websites appear to be flouting the general data protection regulation (GDPR), the strict rules governing how organisations can collect, store and process personal data, according to the research.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Online bookies accused of UK privacy breaches with use of cookie banners

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Tan Dhesi says Argentinian threats make it more crucial than ever that PM increase defence spending
Javier Milei’s threats to the Falkland Islands make it even more important that Andy Burnham increase defence spending immediately, according to the Labour chair of the defence committee.
Tan Dhesi said the comments by the Argentinian president this week show why the government should raise military spending to 3% of GDP by 2030. But he said Burnham’s plans remain mired in confusion after the prime minister appeared to reassure him that the 2030 target would be hit, only for Downing Street to later retreat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falklands row shows urgent need to commit to 3% target, says Labour defence committee chair

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Sources indicate some members states will not enforce EES biometric controls after 6 September deadline

What are the new EU border checks and how will they affect your holiday?

Travellers to the EU could face renewed border queues as flexibility measures for the bloc’s entry-exit system officially come to an end – although numerous sources have indicated that some member states will not enforce biometric checks.
Airlines last week called on the European Commission to extend discretionary powers to pause EES controls when necessary until the end of 2026, with the deadline for “flexibility” passing on 6 September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Travellers to EU face renewed queues as border-check flexibility rules expire

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president suggests he might support his Argentinian ally’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands
Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House.
It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s pique with UK could lead to favor to acolyte Milei over Falklands

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Sector has avoided issue because of stigma fears, expert warns ahead of closure of Nottingham attacks inquiry 
Mental health organisations have “failed to acknowledge” the risk of violence from a minority of people with severe mental illnesses, the chief executive of Mind has said ahead of the closure of the inquiry into the Nottingham attacks.
Dr Sarah Hughes, who has led mental health charity Mind for four years and has worked in the sector for almost four decades, said charities had shied away from addressing the risk of violence due to the fact it had increased the stigma and harassment around people with mental health conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mental health groups have ‘failed to acknowledge’ risk of violence, says Mind chief

articles.author: Taz Ali (now) and Hamish Mackay (earlier)
articles.description:
‘Sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking for it,’ party leader tells gathering in Birmingham 
No real mention by Anderson of the problems that overshadowed events yesterday. He ended his opening speech saying: "Yesterday was great. Today is going to be absolutely brilliant.”
Laila Cunningham is speaking next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage brushes aside Reform controversies in closing conference speech – UK politics as it happened

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
As the government prepares to crack down on ‘phoney bargains’ we ask experts about what exactly constitutes a genuine price reduction
When is a sale not a sale? Online and on the high street, some shops just always seem to be selling at a discount.
Whether it’s the closing down sale that goes on for years, or the crossed-out original price that you can’t remember ever paying, some retailers try all kinds of ways to convince us we are getting a bargain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Deal or no deal? How to know if the retail price is right

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
After bringing injured queen Phoebee home in July, Gilly McArthur expected her soon to die, but she’s bumbling on
Fifty-two days ago, Phoebee was lying by the side of a road in the blistering sun with a broken wing. Today, she’s clambering up the arm of Gilly McArthur, around the nape of her neck and disappearing into her hair.
“I couldn’t leave her by the roadside,” McArthur says. “So I bought her home and made her a bed of flowers. I thought she’d be dead in a day or so.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I could watch her for hours’: the woman who rescued a bee and created a buzz

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
Healthy middle-aged people deemed to be at higher risk of developing condition among those eligible to participate
People without memory loss will be offered an experimental Alzheimer’s drug that could stop the development of the condition before dementia symptoms emerge.
Healthy middle-aged people deemed to have a higher risk of developing the condition will be eligible to participate in the trial, which is being run by an NHS trust as part of an international clinical trial aiming to prevent dementia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alzheimer’s trial to test drug on people without symptoms to see if it can be prevented

articles.author: Chloe Mac Donnell
articles.description:
The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts
For decades shapewear has been used to compress and cinch. But now there is a sub-genre emerging. Rather than shrinking a silhouette, it aims to add inches.
This week M&S launched a bodysuit that features exaggerated padding at the hip allowing the wearer to create an hourglass shape, or at least the illusion of one.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kardashian curves: M&S launches £28 bodysuit with exaggerated hip padding

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Six claims the party has faced – from an undisclosed £5m gift to an alleged plot to bypass election laws
As Reform UK’s annual conference unfolded in Birmingham, the party was once again facing heightened scrutiny over its finances.
Two senior officials have been suspended after they were filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot to get around electoral laws on foreign donations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The two-year trail of financial controversy dogging Reform and Farage

articles.author: Natalie Wint
articles.description:
Experts say invasive species are creating ‘pollinator deserts’ and could have serious impact on food security
British beekeepers have called for a national awareness campaign about the impact of Asian hornets as they warned the invasive species was creating “pollinator deserts” and threatening food security.
Native to south-east Asia, the yellow-legged hornet is thought to have arrived in Europe in 2004 and has continued to spread ever since, its numbers probably boosted by increasingly warm springs and summers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beekeepers warn of Asian hornet threat and call for UK awareness campaign

articles.author: Presented by Michael Safi; produced by George McDonagh and Alex Atack; additional production by Nicola Alexandrou; music and sound design by Rudi Zygadlo; executive producer Joshua Kelly
articles.description:
Across the world, hundreds of people have come to believe they have made extraordinary scientific discoveries with AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Others say their AI has ‘awakened’, or is leading them to a higher spiritual realm. The Guardian journalist Michael Safi investigates a phenomenon labelled ‘AI psychosis’, travelling to the US to meet two people who have been on weird journeys with their chatbots
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black Box: The Chatbots | Spirals | Ep 1 – podcast

articles.description:
Nigel Farage tells Reform UK's annual conference in Birmingham that allegations broadcast by Channel 4 News that his party had breached political donation rules were made because 'they’re scared of us'. The party has suspended two senior officials after they were filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot to get around electoral laws on foreign donations


 Continue reading...
articles.title: 'Reform broke no law': Nigel Farage responds to latest donation revelations – video

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspndent
articles.description:
With senior party figures appearing split and leader’s favourability rating dropping, questions about donations are causing yet more headaches

UK politics live – latest updates

Midway through an event at Reform’s annual conference on Friday there was question for the audience: who was worried about a Channel 4 News exposé of potential wrongdoing by party officials over donations? Almost no hands went up. The faithful might be sanguine. But make no mistake, Nigel Farage faces yet another problem.
Careful plans have been again upset. After months of answering – or primarily dodging – questions about his own finances, Farage had planned to use Reform UK’s biggest conference yet to make a blitz of policy announcements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK exposé comes just as Farage was hoping to change the narrative

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
The potential breaches of the law exposed in an undercover film, what police say, and the party’s likely defence
Nigel Farage is facing yet another finance scandal following an undercover investigation into how Reform UK is funded. The potential wrongdoing – denied by the party – appears serious enough to have been immediately referred to the police by Labour and the Liberal Democrats. Here are the main legal issues for Reform and what any investigation will have to consider.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What is the latest finance scandal facing Reform UK?

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
CCTV footage shows a man jumping from a first-floor window before running into the street and, by chance. approaching a police car. The man jumps in and tells the officer he had been kidnapped and informs him of the location. Lincolnshire police subsequently arrest four men and a woman in connection with the incident
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man dives out of first-floor window to escape kidnappers in Lincolnshire - video

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Steven Morris
articles.description:
Nick Park began modelling the character as a feline, before finding it too difficult and changing him to a dog
The creator of Wallace and Gromit has revealed that the world’s most famous stop-motion animated dog was nearly a cat.
As Aardman Animations marks its 50th anniversary, Nick Park, who joined the studio in 1985, told the BBC he had originally modelled Gromit as a feline companion for Wallace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wallace’s dog Gromit was nearly a cat, reveals creator as Aardman turns 50

articles.author: Daniella Lucas
articles.description:
As one card recently sold for £12m, opportunistic thefts have surged – envelopes are being opened en route, costing small businesses thousands
Pokémon’s success over the last 30 years has seen it grow from a much-loved Game Boy classic, to a world-dominating brand with TV shows, spin-off games, toys and even a theme park. The trading card game is a huge part of that, with more than 85bn cards printed over its lifetime, and the appetite for them shows no signs of slowing down. Packs get snapped up after release so quickly it’s now almost impossible to find them in shops, and a booming resale market is driving the hobby into murky waters.
One card recently sold for an eye-watering £12m, and an increasing number of people have gotten into the collecting business on the hunt for huge profits, leading to a rise in thefts targeting card shops. More recently though, some small businesses have reported that their sales have been hit by thieves targeting envelopes within Royal Mail, leading to thousands in lost revenue.
 Continue reading...

Less than 1% of businesses in England use more water than the daily needs of 10 million people, as millions of households face hosepipe bans and three-quarters of the country is in drought.
Businesses across England use 2.6bn litres a day from the public water supply, which includes potable and non-potable water provided by water companies. In total, businesses account for about 30% of public supply use, with two-thirds of their consumption in water-stressed areas, according to Mosl, the organisation that operates England’s business water market.

Exclusive: Angela Eagle urges UK citizens to be ‘a bit more resilient’ as they plan for national emergencies
British people have been urged to have enough food and water on hand to survive a few days without power or water, as the UN said the El Niño climate phenomenon was “supersizing before our eyes”, exacerbating extreme weather events worldwide.
Forecasters say they are braced for the biggest El Niño in 1,000 years, bringing wildfires and floods to parts of the world, and the threat of a wet, stormy winter for the UK.

 As the British government plans a campaign urging citizens to prepare for national emergencies, Angela Eagle told the Guardian the likelihood of a wild winter showed the importance of keeping supplies at home.

Climate crisis could increase incursions of Aedes aegypti, which can transmit Zika virus and dengue, experts say
A mosquito capable of transmitting tropical diseases has been found breeding in homes in east London, with experts warning that the rapidly warming climate will lead to greater “incursions of invasive mosquitoes”.
This is the first time the species has been identified breeding in the UK and the fourth time it has been detected.

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Gretsch Synchromatic 160 acoustic guitar expected to sell for as much as £120,000, as star lot in auction of items owned by late personal assistant Siobhan Bailey
One of the most iconic items in George Michael’s career, the acoustic guitar he energetically strummed in the video for 1987’s Faith, is going up for auction.
The guitar, a Gretsch Synchromatic 160 with a sunburst finish to the body, has an estimated sale price of £60,000-£120,000. It comes with a case featuring the words Rockabilly Rebel pasted on it – a reference to the twangy, 1950s-referencing sound of Faith, which topped the US charts for four weeks and became a foundation stone of Michael’s post-Wham! solo career.

articles.author: Chris Wiegand Stage editor
articles.description:
Misfits Together, by Bastille’s Dan Smith and To Kill a King’s Ralph Pelleymounter, is set amid the 1950s’ ‘red scare’
It was lampooned as the union of the “hourglass” and the “egghead” – the marriage, in the summer of 1956, between Hollywood superstar Marilyn Monroe and Pulitzer-winning playwright Arthur Miller. Now, a new stage musical is to give a nuanced and intimate portrait of that famous relationship, treat each as trailblazers in their own way and reveal parallels between the volatile state of the US during the 50s “red scare” and now.
The production, which opens next autumn at Leicester’s Curve, is called Misfits Together, a reference to the film Miller wrote for Monroe that was released shortly after their divorce in 1961. It is a foray into musical theatre by two indie musicians, Dan Smith of the band Bastille and Ralph Pelleymounter from To Kill a King, who have recorded the score as a studio album. The first track, Oh America, is out on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New musical to give intimate portrait of Marilyn Monroe and Arthur Miller’s marriage

Reports say Duke and Duchess of Sussex may have returned to Britain due to ‘top secret’ acting role for Meghan – we try to guess what it might be
In 2022, two years after she and Prince Harry bolted to California in an unhappy exit from the royal family, the Duchess of Sussex was asked if she could foresee a return to acting. “No, I’m done,” she told Variety magazine. “I guess never say never, but my intention is to absolutely not.”

More than three weeks after it began burning and two days after the military deployed to the area, there is hope that the huge wildfire on the hillside above the Eastern valley town of Blaenavon may finally be coming under control.
Emergency workers and soldiers described a gruelling battle against the deep-seated peat fire that has spread over 4,000 hectares (9,800 acres), putting lives, farmland and property at risk.

Force has seen busiest month in its history, with heatwaves putting added strain on criminal justice system
On England’s hottest day of the year so far, Ashton-under-Lyne in Greater Manchester was thronging with pedestrians, many clutching ice-creams or cold drinks as they passed through the town centre.
Officers from Greater Manchester police were also out in force, some in plainclothes, some stationed by a facial-recognition van, apprehending wanted suspects and stopping persons of interest. James Green’s oyster company owns a chunk of Whitstable’s shoreline but success has not brought affection from residents
The clink of glasses and the lapping of the tide was punctuated by giggling toddlers and the slurp of oysters at tables populated by people gently sizzling on a baking day on the Kent seaside.
But James Green, of the Whitstable Oyster Fishery Company, had the demeanour of a man who had found grit in his mollusc. “I don’t like to use the term but it is nimbyism,” he said. “Why did it become personal? I don’t know really. Because we’re a family business, it’s a relatively small town?”

Firms are more likely to use technology as ‘the intern in the office’ than as a replacement for skilled staff
Professional designers should not feel “threatened” by the rapid growth of generative AI, according to business leaders, despite fears over job losses in the sector.
With design and film production companies and manufacturers all adopting AI at an accelerating pace, industry bodies said the technology would be used to enhance the work of designers rather than replace them.

Consumers are increasingly encountering AI-generated images on food menus such as leathery meat and bread resembling reptile skin
During a recent lunch break, Jill Sennett saw something so unappetizing she had to share it with her 26,000 X followers: Artificial intelligence-generated menu images from a Jamaican barbecue pop-up restaurant in which the meats looked like leather belts crawling with tiny beetles.
The images were reshared by more than 500 people who similarly expressed their disgust. Eating is “such an essential human experience”, said Sennett, a 37-year-old nurse in Denver. “I think it’s a bad cultural thing that restaurants are converting to these horrific, uncanny food images that are unappetizing.”
